description:
In 1815, a mountain in Indonesia exploded in the most powerful eruption in recorded human history — and for three days, the sun did not rise over parts of Southeast Asia. A year later, it snowed in July in America. This is the story of Tambora: the eruption that erased a kingdom, froze a summer, wrote Frankenstein, and may have helped invent the bicycle.

7:10 History's biggest author

What fascinates me most is how invisible it all was: nobody in 1816 knew why the sun was dim. They just lived through it — and wrote monsters, and rioted for bread, and invented new ways to move. If stories about the hidden gears of history are your thing, subscribe to InkTime.

Watch next: our video "The Library of Alexandria: What We Actually Lost" — what we actually lost when the ancient world's greatest collection of knowledge faded away (link dari tab Konten channel ini). Some losses are loud, like Tambora. Some are silent.
